key_insight: Clipped decentralized SGD achieves order-optimal convergence under heavy-tailed noise while preserving consensus and enabling linear speed-up across agents.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical, scalable training rule for distributed learning systems that need robustness to outlier gradients without sacrificing convergence guarantees.
method: Use local gradient clipping before decentralized SGD updates.
Analyze non-convex smooth objectives under bounded p-th moment noise with p in (1,2].
Show consensus error is higher-order, so network effects do not dominate the rate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both high-probability and expected convergence guarantees, plus numerical experiments that validate the theory.
watch_item: Clipping threshold tuning matters; overly aggressive clipping can bias updates and slow progress if not chosen carefully.
paper_title: Decentralized SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise: Optimal Convergence Rates and the Role of Gradient Clipping
